name: ui/markdown-renderer
title: MarkdownRenderer
summary: Markdown, safe by construction: parsed into a typed tree and drawn as elements, never through an HTML string. Raw HTML in the source is text; links pass a scheme allow-list. One contract for the Astro, React and Mzizi Roots builds.

props.name: content
props.description: The Markdown to show (or, with `from`, rich-text HTML). Untrusted text is fine: it is never parsed as HTML.

props.name: links
props.description: safe keeps http, https, mailto, tel and relative addresses; https keeps https only. A refused link keeps its words and loses its address.

props.name: from
props.description: What content is. html reads an editor's rich text into Markdown first (a reader of its own that builds plain data, never a DOM, so nothing in it runs; the same on a server, in a browser and in Rust); auto does so when the text holds an editor's tags. Text in rich text stays text: Markdown typed into an editor is not read as Markdown.

props.name: headingBase
props.description: The heading level a `#` heading renders at (1 to 6); deeper levels follow and stop at h6. Lets the text sit under a page's own headings.

behaviour: The Markdown is parsed into a typed tree (blocks and inlines) and the tree is rendered as elements. No build has an HTML string sink: no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, no set:html, no dangerous_inner_html.

Blocks: paragraphs (every line break is a hard break), ATX headings, bulleted and numbered lists nested by indentation (a numbered list keeps its first number), blockquotes, fenced code (``` or ~~~, the info word as data-language), horizontal rules and GFM tables with column alignment.
Inlines: code spans, links, bold (** or __), italic (* or _), bold italic (***), backslash escapes. A marker with no partner, and an underscore inside a word, stay text.
Raw HTML in the source is text:

Links: tabs and newlines anywhere, and controls and spaces at either end, are removed first (browsers ignore them), then the scheme is checked against an allow-list. A refused link renders its words with no element around them. http and https links open in a new tab with rel="noopener noreferrer".
A link inside a link's words renders as its words.
Nesting is bounded: lists and blockquotes 8 deep, inline marks 16 deep; deeper markers read as text.
Hostile text stays linear: each inline parse has a scanning budget (100000 steps plus 32 per character); when it runs out, markers still looking for a partner read as text.

Rich text (from=html or auto): block elements and
end lines, source newlines are spaces, list items are one line each, bold, italic, code and links keep their meaning, script-like elements are dropped with their content, and every other tag is a plain container.

rich.description: from=html: an editor's HTML, with Markdown typed into it and a script.

roles: None of its own: the semantic elements (headings, lists, blockquote, table with th scope=col, code) carry the structure.
keyboard: Links are native anchors in reading order.
focus: Links show a focus-visible outline in the ring token.
aria: None needed: the markup is native HTML.

theming.brandOverlay: Links read --primary and their focus outline --ring, so a brand overlay recolours them; nothing else changes.

noJs.without: Everything: the component is server-rendered HTML with no script.

responsive: A wide table or code block scrolls inside itself, not the page.

checks.say: Line breaks are kept in a paragraph.
A nested list sits inside its item.
A numbered list keeps its first number.
An https link opens in a new tab, safely.
A mailto link stays in place.
Only the https link survives the hostile input.
and it is the https one.
Raw HTML in a table cell is text.
and it is the https one.
Empty content renders nothing inside the root.
Markdown typed into rich text is not a heading.
Rich text keeps only its https link.

gaps: Not CommonMark-complete: no setext headings, indented code blocks, reference links, autolinks, footnotes, task lists or strikethrough.
Rich text: tables, images and nested lists in an editor's HTML are read as text (cells and items flattened to lines), not rebuilt.
